text: True or False: If two structures are isomorphic (M ≅ N), then they are elementarily equivalent — they satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences.
explanation: True. Isomorphic structures satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences, so isomorphism implies elementary equivalence. The converse fails: elementarily equivalent structures need not be isomorphic — the standard model of PA and a non-standard model agree on every sentence yet are not isomorphic.
